newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY GRAINS PRICES RESUME SURGE ON MORE RAIN.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY GRAINS PRICES RESUME SURGE ON MORE RAIN.

text.p: Grains prices on Budapest Commodity Exchange futures market resumed their upward surge on Friday as more rain was forecast for the weekend, dealers said.
Milling wheat and feed went limit-up for all maturities while feed wheat for the freed-up month of March rose 1,800 forints.

"The forecast says the weekend is going to be bad again for the harvest," said Gyorgy Varga of OTP Forex. "The wheat is ready for harvest but the combines can't get to the fields so seed is falling to the ground causing a lot of losses."
Varga also said the rain was washing out the glutein content causing a lower proportion of milling wheat in the total crop.
"There's never been such a difference between milling wheat and feed wheat," he said.
Milling wheat positions have soared by over 3,000 forints per tonne in the last week, with a relative pause only on Thursday.
Maize, which is benefiting from the current wet weather conditions, fell for all months except October, which was stable.
"It's the perfect weather for maize, there's a lot of rain in the fields, the ground is moist, so if we're heading for a hot August there's a good chance of a pretty good crop in maize."
Varga said Hungarian farmers always tended to plant 50 percent maize and 50 percent wheat so that losses from one would be compensated by profits from the other.
In Friday's turnover was 742.6 million forints, most trade was in milling wheat, with August, which rose 240 to 25,240, and December which rose 430 to 28,130 forints, seeing the most deals.
Most of the light turnover in feed wheat was for December, which rose limit-up 400 forints to 19,850 forints, and March which rose 1800 to 22,000.
Maize turnover was spread between December, March, May and next July, with all four months falling limit-down to 18,700, 19,600, 20,390 and 21,200 respectively.
